name: long-history-scale

files.README.md:
# Catalog import

Suppliers upload catalog files, the reader parses them, the validator checks
them against the catalog schema, and accepted rows are written to the store.

history.task: Debug catalog files that fail on their very first line
history.summary: Every failing file came out of a Windows editor: the first header cell carried a byte-order mark, so the column name never matched the schema and the whole file was rejected as unknown.

history.task: Make the reader tolerate a leading marker on the header line
history.summary: The reader now strips the byte-order mark before the header row is parsed, so files saved by desktop editors load without any manual cleanup step.

history.task: Settle where character decoding belongs in the pipeline
history.summary: Agreed that decoding happens in the reader, never in the validator, so the validator only ever sees normalised text and its rules stay about content rather than about bytes.
decisions: Decoding belongs to the reader; the validator receives normalised text only

history.task: Add regression coverage for the marked header case
history.summary: Added an encoding regression suite that feeds a marked file through the whole pipeline and asserts the header maps cleanly onto the catalog columns.

history.task: Speed up the duplicate SKU check
history.summary: Replaced the per-row lookup with a single set built up front, which cut the duplicate check from minutes to seconds on a large catalog.

history.task: Report every validation error instead of only the first
history.summary: The validator collects every problem in a file and returns them together, so a supplier fixes one upload instead of ten.

history.task: Accept semicolon delimited files
history.summary: Delimiter detection samples the opening lines, so semicolon files from European suppliers load without a manual conversion.
decisions: Delimiter detection samples the first five lines and never guesses from the file extension

history.task: Trim trailing whitespace from every cell
history.summary: Cells are trimmed on read, which removed a long tail of spurious mismatches on supplier product names.

history.task: Add a dry run flag to the import command
history.summary: The import command takes a dry run flag that checks a file and prints the report without writing any rows.

history.task: Investigate a stuck import job
history.summary: The stuck job was waiting on a database lock held by a long reporting query; killing the report let it finish, but the locking pattern is unchanged.

history.task: Document the supplier column mapping
history.summary: Wrote down how supplier column names map onto catalog fields so support can answer mapping questions without reading code.

edits.docs/mapping.md:
# Supplier column mapping

| Supplier column | Catalog field |
| --- | --- |
| Artikelnummer | sku |
| Bezeichnung | name |

history.task: Reject files larger than fifty megabytes
history.summary: Uploads above fifty megabytes are turned away up front with a clear message instead of timing out halfway through.

history.task: Fix the price rounding on discounted items
history.summary: Discounted prices are rounded once at the end instead of at each step, which removed the one cent drift suppliers kept reporting.

history.task: Retry the catalog write on a transient database error
history.summary: The catalog write retries three times on a transient error before giving up, which cleared most of the nightly noise.

history.task: Move import logs into their own table
history.summary: Import logs live in their own table now, so a failed run can be inspected without scanning the application log.

history.task: Add a progress endpoint for long imports
history.summary: A progress endpoint reports how many rows were processed and how many were turned away while a run is still going.

history.task: Investigate a memory spike on very wide files
history.summary: Could not pin down the memory spike on files with three hundred columns; the profile was dominated by the parser but nothing obvious stood out.

history.task: Normalise supplier names before matching
history.summary: Supplier names are lowercased and stripped of punctuation before matching, which cut the unmatched rate noticeably.

history.task: Let support re-run a failed import
history.summary: Support can re-run a failed import from the console with the original upload, which removed most of the back and forth with suppliers.

history.task: Cache the schema between imports
history.summary: The schema loads once per process instead of once per file, which removed a visible pause at the start of every run.
decisions: The catalog schema is cached per process and reloaded only on deploy

history.task: Tighten the currency field rules
history.summary: The currency field is checked against a fixed list of codes, and a bad code is reported together with the offending row number.

history.task: Split the importer into reader and writer packages
history.summary: The importer is split so the parser can be exercised without a database, which made those tests much faster.

history.task: Warn when a file has no rows
history.summary: An empty upload produces a warning and a zero row report instead of a silent success.

history.task: Back-fill the missing product images
history.summary: Back-filled images for most products; a few hundred remain because their supplier links are dead, and that list went to the catalog team.

history.task: Make the price column accept a comma decimal separator
history.summary: Prices written with a comma decimal separator are accepted now, which is how most continental suppliers export their sheets.

history.task: Send a summary mail when a run finishes
history.summary: A short mail goes out at the end of every run with counts and a link to the log, which replaced the manual check people were doing.

history.task: Drop the unused legacy import endpoint
history.summary: Removed the legacy endpoint nobody had called in six months, along with its tests and its entry in the routing table.

history.task: Investigate slow writes during the evening batch
history.summary: Evening writes are slow because the batch overlaps the analytics export; measured it, but did not change the schedule.
